Pack ids are kept from the German trainer (they are slots: progress keys and i18n keys praep.pack.<id>); the English topic of each is its name. cat "wechsel" = also listed under "Place and movement" in the rail. Question: prompt with ___, options (exactly one correct), answer, explain, change (chip after the answer).

rule.text: at for clock times and a few short phrases, on for days and dates, in for months, years, seasons and parts of the day. No preposition before this, next, last, every, today, tomorrow, yesterday: next Monday, last year.

table.caption: at, on, in for time
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: at 7 o'clock, at night, at lunchtime
on Monday, on 3 May, on my birthday
months, years, seasons, parts of the day
in July, in 2024, in winter, in the morning

questions.prompt: The film starts ___ 8 o'clock.
I was born ___ 1998.
We have English ___ Mondays.
questions.explain: on + a day of the week.

questions.prompt: My birthday is ___ June.
I don't sleep well ___ night.
questions.explain: at night – but in the morning, in the evening.

questions.prompt: I always drink coffee ___ the morning.
questions.explain: in + the morning / the afternoon / the evening.

questions.prompt: The shop is closed ___ Christmas Day.
questions.explain: Christmas Day is one day: on + a day.

questions.prompt: It's very cold here ___ winter.
The meeting is ___ 14 March.
I finish work ___ half past five.
We're leaving ___ Friday morning.
questions.explain: A day + part of the day takes on: on Friday morning.

questions.prompt: She called me ___ lunchtime.
questions.explain: at + a mealtime: at lunchtime, at dinner.

rule.text: in = inside a space: a room, a box, a town, a country. on = on a surface: a table, a wall, the floor, a page. at = at a point, or at a place where something happens: at the bus stop, at work, at a party.

table.caption: in, on, at for place
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: on the table, on the wall, on page 5
a point; a place for an activity
at the bus stop, at work, at a party

questions.prompt: Your keys are ___ the table.
My parents live ___ Manchester.
questions.explain: in + a town or a country.

questions.prompt: Wait for me ___ the bus stop.
questions.explain: at + a point: at the bus stop, at the door.

questions.prompt: There's a picture ___ the wall.
questions.explain: A wall is a surface: on the wall.

questions.prompt: The milk is ___ the fridge.
I'm ___ work until six.
questions.explain: at work, at school, at home.

questions.prompt: The answer is ___ page 12.
We met ___ a party.
questions.explain: at + an event: at a party, at a concert.

questions.prompt: The children are playing ___ the garden.
questions.explain: A garden is an area with borders: in the garden.

questions.prompt: Someone is ___ the door.
questions.explain: at the door = just outside it.

questions.prompt: Mei is cooking ___ the kitchen.
There's a cat ___ the roof.
questions.explain: on top of a surface: on the roof.

packs.name: Time: before, after, from … to, until

rule.text: before = earlier than. after = later than. from … to (or from … until) gives the start and the end. until = all the time up to a point, then it stops.

table.caption: before, after, from … to, until
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: from 9 to 5, from Monday to Friday
up to a time, then it stops

questions.prompt: The shop is open ___ 9 am to 6 pm.
questions.explain: from … to: the start and the end.

questions.prompt: The shop is open from 9 am ___ 6 pm.
I'm at work ___ 5 o'clock. Then I go home.
questions.explain: until = up to that time, then it stops.

questions.prompt: Please arrive ten minutes ___ the start.
___ work, I usually go to the gym.
We waited ___ midnight, but she didn't come.
questions.explain: until = all the time up to then.

questions.prompt: I work ___ Monday to Friday.
I'm on holiday from 1 August ___ 15 August.
Do your homework ___ dinner, then you can watch TV.
questions.explain: First homework, then TV: before dinner.

questions.prompt: It rained ___ morning to night.
questions.explain: from morning to night = all day.

questions.prompt: Call me ___ the meeting and tell me how it went.
questions.explain: You can only say how it went when it's over: after.

questions.prompt: The café is open ___ late.
questions.explain: open until late = it closes late.

rule.text: go / come / drive / fly + to for movement to a place: go to work, fly to Rome. at or in for where you are: at work, at the station, in Paris. No preposition before home: go home, come home – but be at home.

table.caption: to, at, in
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: go to school, fly to Rome
where you are: a point or a building
at school, at the station, at home
where you are: a town, a country, a room
in Paris, in Spain, in bed
no preposition before home, here, there

questions.prompt: I go ___ work by bus.
She's ___ work today.
questions.explain: be at work = where you are.

questions.prompt: We're flying ___ Rome tomorrow.
My brother lives ___ Spain.
The children go ___ school at eight.
Are you ___ home this evening?
questions.explain: be at home – but go home, with no preposition.

questions.prompt: Welcome ___ Brighton!
I'll meet you ___ the airport.
questions.explain: Where you meet: at the airport.

questions.prompt: How do I get ___ the station?
We arrived ___ London at six.
questions.explain: arrive in + a town or a country. Never arrive to.

questions.prompt: We arrived ___ the hotel late.
questions.explain: arrive at + a building or a place.

questions.prompt: Kwame went ___ the doctor's yesterday.

packs.name: Where is it? next to, behind, between …
packs.preps: next to · behind · in front of · between · opposite · under · above

rule.text: These say where something is. between = in the middle of two things. opposite = on the other side, facing it. in front of is on the same side: the car in front of the house.

table.caption: Where is it?
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: The bank is next to the café.
The garden is behind the house.
at the front of, on the same side
The car is in front of the house.
in the middle of two things
The chemist's is between the bank and the café.
The school is opposite the park.
The cat is under the bed. The light is above the door.

questions.prompt: The chemist's is ___ the bank and the café.
questions.explain: between A and B = in the middle.
questions.change: between the bank and the café

questions.prompt: We have a small garden at the back. The garden is ___ the house.
Park ___ the house, by the front door.
questions.explain: by the front door = in front of.

questions.prompt: The school is on the other side of the road, ___ the park.
questions.explain: on the other side, facing it = opposite.

questions.prompt: There's a lamp ___ the table, hanging from the ceiling.
The dog is lying ___ the table, out of the sun.
Come and sit ___ me on the sofa.
The car park is ___ the supermarket, at the back.
Write your name ___ the line, not under it.
Wait ___ the cinema, at the entrance.
questions.explain: at the entrance = in front of.

questions.prompt: The town hall is ___ the church and the library.
questions.explain: between + two things joined with and.
questions.change: between the church and the library

questions.prompt: Your shoes are on the floor ___ the bed.
questions.explain: on the floor, below the bed = under.

packs.name: Movement: into, through, across …
packs.preps: into · out of · through · across · along · past · up · down

rule.text: These say where something moves. into = entering (go into the room); in = place (be in the room). through = in one side and out the other (a tunnel, a forest). across = from one side to the other of a flat area (a road, a river).

table.caption: Movement
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: She ran into the shop. He came out of the bank.
in one side, out the other
The train goes through a tunnel.
from one side to the other
Go up the stairs. Run down the hill.

questions.prompt: She jumped ___ the pool and swam to the other side.
The train goes ___ a long tunnel.
questions.explain: In one end and out the other: through.

questions.prompt: Be careful when you go ___ the road.
questions.explain: From one side of the road to the other: across.

questions.prompt: We walked ___ the river for an hour.
questions.explain: Following the line of the river: along.

questions.prompt: Go ___ the church and turn left after it.
questions.explain: Going by it, not into it: past.

questions.prompt: He took his phone ___ his pocket.
Climb ___ the stairs to the top floor.
The ball rolled ___ the hill to the bottom.
Get ___ the car, quick! It's raining.
questions.explain: Get into the car to stay dry.

questions.prompt: A bird flew ___ the open window into the room.
The cat ran ___ the garden to the other side.
questions.explain: From one side to the other: across.

questions.prompt: The thief ran ___ the bank and jumped into a car.

packs.name: Place or movement? in or into, at or to
packs.preps: in · into · on · onto · at · to

rule.text: Place (where is it?): in, on, at. Movement (where does it go?): into, onto, to. In speech, in and on are also used for movement (Put it in the box), but into, onto and to are never used for place: I'm in the kitchen, not into the kitchen.

table.caption: Place or movement?
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: I'm in the kitchen. Come into the kitchen.
on a surface / moving onto it
The cup is on the table. The cat jumped onto the table.
at a place / going to it
We were at the cinema. We went to the cinema.

questions.prompt: I'm ___ the kitchen. Come and help me.
She went ___ the bank to get some money.
questions.explain: Movement to a place: go to.

questions.prompt: We were ___ the cinema last night.
He fell ___ the river and got wet.
The keys are ___ the box.
Let's go ___ the beach this afternoon.
There were a lot of people ___ the concert.
The cat jumped ___ the table.
questions.explain: Movement up onto a surface: onto.

questions.prompt: Your book is ___ the shelf.
I'll drive you ___ the airport.
questions.explain: Movement: drive somebody to a place.

questions.prompt: Wait for me ___ the entrance.
The thief ran ___ the shop and out of the back door.

packs.name: Fixed phrases: by bus, on foot, at home

rule.text: Transport: by + vehicle with no article (by bus, by car), but on foot. With a / the / my: on the bus, on the train, in my car, in a taxi. Fixed phrases: at home, at work, in bed, in hospital (UK), on holiday. Payment and messages: by card, by email.

table.caption: Fixed phrases
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: how you travel or send (no article)
by bus, by plane, by email, by card
buses, trains, planes; on foot; on holiday
on the train, on foot, on holiday
cars and taxis; in bed, in hospital

questions.prompt: I go to work ___ bus.
We didn't take the car. We went ___ foot.
questions.explain: on foot – the one exception to by.

questions.prompt: I read a book ___ the bus.
questions.explain: on the bus / on the train / on the plane.

questions.prompt: She came home ___ taxi.
questions.explain: No article: by taxi. With an article: in a taxi.

questions.prompt: Get ___ my car, I'll drive you.
Sorry, Liam is still ___ bed.
Is Priya ___ home?
My grandfather is ___ hospital after his operation.
questions.explain: in hospital (UK, no article; US: in the hospital).

questions.prompt: We're going ___ holiday next week.
I'll send the documents ___ email.
Do you want to pay ___ card?
questions.explain: pay by card – but in cash.

questions.prompt: Is there Wi-Fi ___ the train?

packs.name: Verbs + prepositions: about, at, for, to

rule.text: Many verbs need a fixed preposition. Learn them as one unit: wait for, look at, listen to, talk about. After the preposition use a noun, a pronoun or -ing: I'm thinking about moving.

table.caption: Verbs + about, at, for, to
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: wait, look, pay, ask, apply for
listen, talk, belong to; explain sth to sb

questions.prompt: Who are you waiting ___?
Listen ___ me, please.
Look ___ this photo – it's me as a child!
I'm looking ___ my glasses. Have you seen them?
We talked ___ the new project for an hour.
Who paid ___ the drinks?
This phone belongs ___ Zofia.
Don't worry ___ the exam. You'll be fine.
Everyone laughed ___ his joke.
She applied ___ a job at the hospital.
Can you explain the rule ___ me again?
questions.explain: explain something to somebody (not explain me).

questions.prompt: He complained ___ the cold food.

packs.name: Verbs + prepositions: on, of, in, from, with

rule.text: More verbs with a fixed preposition. Some look strange from your own language, so learn the pair: depend on (not depend of), consist of, believe in, agree with.

table.caption: Verbs + on, of, in, from, with
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: depend, rely, concentrate on; spend money on
think of (opinion), consist of, dream of
What do you think of it?
agree, deal with; help somebody with

questions.prompt: It depends ___ the price.
I agree ___ you completely.
What do you think ___ my new jacket?
questions.explain: think of = have an opinion about.

questions.prompt: Do you believe ___ ghosts?
Have you heard ___ Mei recently?
questions.explain: hear from somebody = get news from them.

questions.prompt: He suffers ___ back pain.
questions.explain: suffer from an illness or a problem.

questions.prompt: You can always rely ___ me.
The course consists ___ ten lessons.
Fifty people took part ___ the race.
Can you help me ___ my bags?
I can't concentrate ___ my work with this noise.
Can I borrow a pen ___ you?

packs.name: Time: for, since, during, by, until

rule.text: for + a length of time (how long?), since + a point in time (from when?), usually with the present perfect. during + a noun (during the film), not a number of hours. by = not later than; until = all the time up to then.

table.caption: for, since, during, by, until
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: for two hours, for ten years
in the time of an event
during the film, during the night
up to a time, then it stops

questions.prompt: I've lived here ___ 2015.
I've lived here ___ ten years.
My phone rang ___ the meeting.
Please send me the report ___ Friday at the latest.
The shop is open ___ 10 pm.
questions.explain: until = up to then, then it closes.

questions.prompt: We waited ___ an hour, but the bus didn't come.
She has been ill ___ last week.
Nobody spoke ___ the film.
I'll be back ___ six, so we can have dinner then.
We stayed at the party ___ midnight.
questions.explain: until = the whole time up to midnight.

questions.prompt: It rained ___ three days without stopping.
I haven't seen him ___ we left school.

packs.name: Adjectives + prepositions
packs.preps: at · of · in · about · with · for

rule.text: Many adjectives have their own preposition: good at, afraid of, interested in. After the preposition use a noun, a pronoun or -ing: I'm good at cooking.

table.caption: Adjectives + prepositions
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: afraid of, proud of, tired of, full of
famous for, responsible for, late for

questions.prompt: I'm not very good ___ cooking.
My little brother is afraid ___ the dark.
Are you interested ___ art?
I'm really excited ___ the trip.
Sorry, I'm late ___ the meeting.
Liverpool is famous ___ its music.
We're very proud ___ our daughter.
My mum was angry ___ me because I came home late.
I'm tired ___ waiting. Let's go.
The box was full ___ old photos.
Who is responsible ___ this mess?
Are you worried ___ your exam?

packs.name: Formal prepositions: due to, despite, instead of …
packs.preps: according to · apart from · despite · due to · in spite of · instead of · owing to · thanks to

rule.text: These work like prepositions, so a noun or -ing follows: despite the rain, instead of waiting. Not a full clause: despite it rained ✗ → although it rained, or despite the fact that it rained.

table.caption: Formal prepositions
head: Preposition
Use
Example
rows: The train was late due to the snow.
Despite the rain, we went out.
According to the forecast, it will rain.
Thanks to your help, we finished.

questions.prompt: The flight was cancelled ___ bad weather.
___ the rain, the match went ahead.
Can I have water ___ wine, please?
___ the weather forecast, it will snow tomorrow.
___ your help, we finished on time.
questions.explain: thanks to = because of (a good result).

questions.prompt: Everyone came to the party ___ Liam, who was ill.
She went to work ___ feeling ill.
The road is closed ___ an accident.
He watched TV ___ doing his homework.
___ a few small mistakes, your essay is excellent.
We enjoyed the trip ___ the long delays.
___ the police, the driver was going too fast.
questions.explain: according to = this is what they say.

packs.name: Nouns + prepositions: reason for, rise in …
packs.preps: for · in · to · on · of · with

rule.text: Nouns have fixed prepositions too, and they are often different from the verb's: increase in prices (but prices increase), effect on, answer to, reason for. Learn the noun and its preposition together.

questions.prompt: What's the reason ___ the delay?
There has been a sharp increase ___ prices.
Nobody knows the answer ___ this question.
Stress can have a big effect ___ your health.
One advantage ___ living in a city is the transport.
questions.change: advantage of living in a city

questions.prompt: We have a problem ___ the heating.
Thank you for the invitation ___ your wedding.
There is a growing demand ___ electric cars.
The police are still looking for the cause ___ the fire.
Is there a solution ___ the problem?
The new law will have an impact ___ small businesses.
My relationship ___ my sister is much better now.
